standard.title: First Nations music and cultural continuity
standard.description: explore ways First Nations Australians use music to continue and revitalise culture
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored how First Nations Australians use music to communicate connection to and responsibility for Country/Place (AC9AMU4E02), including engaging with First Nations Australian voices directly. The new focus is cultural continuity and revitalisation — music's role in maintaining living culture, language, and knowledge, including in contemporary contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore ways First Nations Australians use music to continue and revitalise culture, investigating diverse styles, language preservation, and how cultural knowledge is shared through performance.

nodes.label: Diverse contemporary styles and instruments
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate the diverse music styles and instruments that living First Nations Australian composers and performers are using, including in contemporary genres.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two different music styles or genres being used by living First Nations Australian composers or performers; describe one instrument or musical feature of each.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate the range of music styles used by living First Nations Australian composers and performers — contemporary pop, hip-hop, classical, orchestral, ceremonial, folk; identify instruments including both traditional instruments and contemporary ones; recognise the diversity of what First Nations Australian music is and can be.
wider: Compare a First Nations Australian artist working in a contemporary genre (e.g. hip-hop or pop) with one working in a more traditional context — describe how each serves cultural continuity in different ways
Investigate the work of a specific First Nations Australian composer or performer in depth — identify their style, instruments, cultural context and what they say about their music
nodes.hinge_reason: A narrow image of what First Nations Australian music 'is' — limited to traditional or ceremonial contexts — prevents students from engaging with living cultural continuity. If students associate First Nations Australian music only with the past, they cannot understand how music continues and revitalises culture in the present. This conceptual block makes the rest of the descriptor inaccessible.

response_modes.reason: Deliberately expose students to First Nations Australian musicians working across diverse contemporary genres alongside traditional contexts. The breadth itself challenges the assumption that First Nations Australian music is a single, historical thing — each new genre context adds evidence for living, diverse cultural expression.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The diversity of contemporary First Nations Australian music is genuinely surprising and rich — students who discover hip-hop, orchestral music, and contemporary pop alongside traditional music encounter a much more complex and compelling picture of living culture.
success_criteria: Can name at least two different music styles used by living First Nations Australian artists
Can describe how each style is connected to First Nations Australian identity or cultural expression

nodes.label: Language revitalisation through music
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe how music is being used to maintain and revitalise knowledge and use of First Nations Australian languages.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one example of First Nations Australian music that uses or teaches a specific language; describe how the music contributes to language knowledge.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate how First Nations Australian musicians are using music to maintain and revitalise languages — songs that teach vocabulary, performances that model pronunciation and usage, recordings that preserve language from Elders; discuss the role music plays in keeping languages alive that might otherwise be lost.
wider: Research a specific First Nations Australian language that music is helping to revitalise — find and listen to examples of that music, then discuss how music serves language learning differently from formal instruction
Investigate how musicians balance the use of English and First Nations Australian languages in their music — what choices do they make and why?

response_modes.reason: Language revitalisation through music is a concept most students will encounter for the first time at Y5-6. Build understanding through specific examples and guided questioning: 'How does singing a song in a language help you learn that language?' 'Why might music be a more effective vehicle for language preservation than textbooks?' Connect to what students know about how music helps people remember things.

success_criteria: Can describe at least one way music is being used to maintain or revitalise a First Nations Australian language
Can explain why music serves this purpose effectively

nodes.label: Sharing cultural knowledge through performance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe how First Nations Australian composers and performers share cultural knowledge as part of their performances — including acknowledgements and explanations.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one way a First Nations Australian performer shares cultural knowledge as part of a performance (e.g. acknowledging Country/Place, sharing language information, explaining inspiration).
nodes.typical_width: Investigate how First Nations Australian composers and performers share cultural knowledge in performances — acknowledging Country/Place before performing, sharing information about the language used in a song, explaining the inspiration for a composition, connecting the music to specific cultural stories or knowledge; discuss what this practice communicates to audiences.
wider: Compare how cultural knowledge is shared in two different performance contexts (e.g. a mainstream festival vs a community ceremony) — what is shared in each, and what is different?
Investigate how First Nations Australian musicians who create music for animations or screen works incorporate cultural knowledge into the work itself — analyse one specific example in depth

response_modes.reason: This node integrates the understanding of living cultural diversity with language revitalisation and the specific practice of knowledge-sharing in performance. It brings the exploration of First Nations Australian cultural continuity together in the concrete act of a performer choosing to make their cultural knowledge part of the performance event.

success_criteria: Can identify at least one way a First Nations Australian performer shares cultural knowledge in a performance
Can explain what that practice communicates to audiences about culture and identity
